title: Seller Quickcase: Battle Brief (draft)
content:
Deck purpose: ultra-compact runbook for SEs to 1) qualify pilot fit fast, 2) win technical trust in 15m, 3) escalate smoothly to a Dedicated commitment.

Slide 1 — One-liner value prop: Redwood makes inference predictable: latency SLAs, cost levers, and graceful fallbacks across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
Speaker note: open with customer pain — ‘we outgrow API unpredictability’ story.

Slide 2 — 3 pilot signals we need in discovery (yes/no quick checks):
- Per-session p95 latency target? (yes -> call latency SLO flow)
- Data residency constraints? (yes -> private/VPC path)
- Peak qps burst pattern? (spiky -> recommend reserved pause/burst config)

Slide 3 — Quick objection scripts (30s):
- ‘Open models are cheaper’ -> "we recommend model + quantization profile that preserves output quality; show unit cost delta and the fallback cost cap"
- ‘Latency spikes on day 2’ -> "prefix caching + autoscale+fallback combo — demoflow and rollback steps"

Slide 4 — Fallback recipe (operational):
- Primary: low-latency hosted variant (quantized)
- Secondary: cheaper throughput variant (batched)
- Triage: enable live trace link + flag for auto-fallback
TODO: get SRE runbook ID to link here.

Slide 5 — Pricing levers to propose in negotiation (talk track + numbers placeholder):
- Trial credit + capped overage for pilot (default 30 days)
- If sustained p95 < target -> convert to reserved capacity credit structure
- Enterprise add-on: extended retention + SLA for X% uplift

Slide 6 — Pilot -> Dedicated conversion checklist (SE playbook):
- Confirm steady-state QPS and token mix (sample 3 days)
- Confirm model pin/version and regression evals (pass threshold?)
- Propose reserved pool size + burst policy + rollback SLA
- Draft SOW + timeline (2–4 weeks)

Slide 7 — Quick role cues for live demo (3 bullets):
- SE: instrument trace and show live KV cache hit rate
- PM/Buyer: show cost projection sheet (2–3 buckets)
- Ops: review network & firewall checklist for private/VPC

Slide 8 — Risk radar (what to monitor post-pilot):
- Model drift signals (accuracy vs baseline prompts)
- Latency regressions at tail during growth (p95->p99)
- Cost levers triggered by bursty traffic

Slide 9 — Short scripts and snippets (copyable):
- Qualify intro: "What does a slow or unpredictable inference call cost you in user ops or revenue?"
- Close nudges: "If we can guarantee X ms p95 and cap your spend at Y, would you be open to a committed pool?"

Slide 10 — Open questions + action items (notes to self):
- Get updated quantization benchmarks from Applied ML (priority).
- Add cheat graph: latency vs cost for 3 reference models.
- Draft 2-line CFO email template for pilot overage justification.

Rough appendix: sample pilot KPI template (table form -- paste into spreadsheet):
- metric, baseline, goal, measurement window, owner, alert threshold
- e.g., p95 latency, 420ms, 200ms, 24h rolling, infra-owner, alert p95>300ms

Unresolved: dispute resolution for hallucination incidents during pilot (need legal + product input).

Style notes: short bullets, copyable scripts, heavy on actionable next steps. This is intentionally rough — meant for SEs to fork into a 10-slide live deck.

References: link to experiment folder (internal, will attach), convo thread in #g2m-pilot-runbooks, and GH PR above.

Sign off: Maya (owner) — ping Jordan for numbers, Diego for fallback runbook links.
